messages:
Alyssa: bringing up a new HF model in onboarding CI — tokenization mismatch causing eval failures, looks like our fast loader isn't picking up the tokenizer artifacts
Sam: can you paste the CI snippet / error?
Alyssa: runtime log: `Could not find tokenizer.json, falling back to slow` even though upstream bundle includes tokenizer.json and vocab files
Alyssa: also `tokenizer_config.json` references `tokenizer_class: CustomFastTokenizer` which our runtime doesn't implement
Marco: ok that explains it — the conversion wrote tokenizer.json but left tokenizer_config pointing at a custom wrapper class name
Iris: what's the observed user impact? eval metrics?
Alyssa: QA baseline -> multi-turn LM evals jumped, BLEU down ~4 points and token alignment differs in canonical sentence checks
Alyssa: repro locally: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('models/foo'); print(t.encode('Hello world'))"` yields different ids on upstream HF vs our runtime
Ops-bot: Note: our runtime expects either a full tokenizer.json produced by tokenizers lib or an explicit mapping in tokenizer_config.json. Missing referenced files cause fast-load to abort
Marco: quick mitigation — sanitize tokenizer_config so `tokenizer_class` maps to `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` or drop unknown entries during import
Sam: watchouts: if special tokens are split into `special_tokens_map.json` or `added_tokens.json`, the fast loader needs them present; HF python will sometimes synthesize missing pieces but our Rust loader doesn't
Alyssa: root cause for this bundle: conversion omitted `special_tokens_map.json`, and tokenizer_config.json still referenced a `preprocessor_class` that pointed to a missing artifact. fast loader bails early
Iris: can the converter emit a minimal `special_tokens_map.json` when missing? something like `{"unk_token":"<unk>","pad_token":"<pad>"}`
Alyssa: yes temporary patch uploaded to model registry with tiny `special_tokens_map.json` and sanitized tokenizer_config. kicking CI
Marco: I'll add a pre-flight check in the importer: validate tokenizer_config keys against present files and fail with a clear message instead of silent fallback
Sam: also add an onboarding eval that tokenizes a canonical sentence and compares token ids against HF python to detect divergence early
Alyssa: runtime error we saw: `error: tokenizer_config.json refers to preprocessor_class but no preprocessor file found; fast load failed, slow fallback used`
Marco: follow-up doc: devex should have a one-pager listing required artifacts for fast-tokenizer loader (tokenizer.json OR vocab+merges, plus special_tokens_map if used, and no unknown tokenizer_class)
Iris: filing ticket for converter change + CI check + devex doc
Alyssa: filed ML-428, pushed conversion patch and conversion-note.txt into the model bundle
Sam: re-run CI once the patched bundle lands, ping here when green
Alyssa: done — CI kicked, will report back. Thanks all :thumbsup:
